empty.title: Give your agent hands
empty.body: Connections are the tools your agents can call — email, calendars, databases, your own servers. Pick how you want to connect.
empty.encryption: Keys and tokens are encrypted with your master passkey — the same one guarding your model keys. Nothing is stored in plain text and nothing leaves this device except calls you configure.

status.lockedHint: Unlock with your master passkey to use this connection.
status.bridgeDownHint: The local server isn't reachable. Start the bridge command again.
status.incompleteHint: Your key is saved. Connect at least one app to finish.

composio.name: Composio
composio.body: One API key, 250+ apps. Sign in to Gmail or Slack the normal way — Composio holds the OAuth, we never see your passwords.

template.name: Local server
template.body: Run a published MCP package against your own machine — filesystem, git, Postgres, Puppeteer. Pick a template, fill in the blanks.
template.bridgeWarning: In the extension this needs one terminal command to bridge. The desktop app runs it for you.
template.nativeNote: Runs on your machine, no terminal needed.
template.notBuiltTitle: Local servers are not ready yet
template.notBuiltBody: This lane will let you pick a published MCP package and fill in its settings. Until then, run the server yourself and add it as a custom endpoint.

custom.name: Custom endpoint
custom.body: Any MCP server you can reach over HTTP or SSE. Set headers, bearer tokens, timeouts, and choose which tools to expose.

detail.deleteConfirm: Delete this connection? Agents using it will lose its tools.

composio.apiKeyHint: Find it under Settings → Project Settings at platform.composio.dev
composio.encryptionNote: Encrypted with your master passkey before it touches disk. You will be asked for the passkey once per browser session — the same prompt that unlocks your model keys.
composio.explainerBody: It holds the OAuth for each app and hands your agent a single tool endpoint. You sign in to Gmail on Google's own page. Memorall stores your Composio key; Composio stores the app tokens; neither of us sees your password.
composio.keyInvalid: That key was rejected by Composio. Check you copied the whole project key.
composio.waitingBody: We opened {{app}}'s authorization page in a new tab. This panel updates by itself the moment you approve.
composio.toolsBeforeScoping: {{apps}} apps connected · {{tools}} tools available before scoping
composio.scopeSubtitle: fewer, sharper tools make a better agent
composio.willAdd: {{count}} tools will be added to your agents' toolbox
composio.webUnsupported: Composio needs the browser extension or the desktop app — the web build can't reach their API directly.

template.title: Local server
template.runOnce: Run this once in a terminal
template.runOnceBody: Browser extensions can't start local processes, so this command bridges the server onto a URL we can reach. Leave it running while you use the agent.
template.portBusy: Port {{port}} looks busy. We picked {{suggested}} instead.
template.bridgeUnreachable: Nothing is answering on that port yet
template.keepChecking: Memorall will keep checking this URL and tell you when the bridge stops.
template.approveBody: It runs as you, with access to {{scope}}. It stops when you quit Memorall or disable the connection.

custom.title: Add custom endpoint
custom.subtitle: Any MCP server reachable over HTTP or SSE
custom.extraHeadersHint: Non-secret headers only — credentials belong in the field above.
custom.enableByDefault: Enable for new agents by default

agent.label: Connections
agent.modalSubtitle: Enable what this agent may use. Scoping is per agent.
agent.newConnectionHint: opens the same three lanes, here
agent.tooMany: That's a lot of tools for one agent — consider narrowing the scope.
